raw_results.question: Find the top 5 articles with the highest in-degree / out-degree ratio based on CITED relationships, excluding any article with out-degree 0. Report only the titles as a list of strings and nothing else.

parameters.query:
MATCH (a:Article)
OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-[:CITED]->(:Article)
WITH a, count(*) AS outDeg
OPTIONAL MATCH (:Article)-[:CITED]->(a)
WITH a, outDeg, count(*) AS inDeg
WHERE outDeg > 0
WITH a.title AS title, toFloat(inDeg) / outDeg AS ratio
ORDER BY ratio DESC, title ASC
LIMIT 5
RETURN title

raw_results.question: Find the longest citation chain (path) between any two articles following outgoing CITED edges. Report only the length as a number and nothing else.

parameters.cypherQuery:
MATCH (n:Article)-[r:CITED]->(m:Article)
RETURN gds.graph.project(
 $graph_name,
 n,
 m,
 {
  sourceNodeLabels: labels(n),
  targetNodeLabels: labels(m),
  relationshipType: type(r)
 }
)

raw_results.question: Build the co-authorship graph where two authors are connected (undirected, unweighted) if they co-authored at least one article. Using the Adamic Adar measure, score the likelihood of future collaboration between Chao Zhang and each of their 2nd-degree co-authors — people who share a 1st-degree co-author with Chao Zhang but have never directly co-authored with them. Report only the top 3 names as a list of strings, breaking ties by name ascending and nothing else.

parameters.query:
MATCH (ch:Author {name: $name})
// Build candidate set: authors at 2 hops in co-author graph via shared first-degree coauthors
MATCH (a1:Article)-[:AUTHOR]->(ch)
MATCH (a1)-[:AUTHOR]->(co1:Author)
WHERE co1 <> ch
MATCH (a2:Article)-[:AUTHOR]->(co1)
MATCH (a2)-[:AUTHOR]->(cand:Author)
WHERE cand <> ch AND cand <> co1
WITH ch, collect(DISTINCT cand) AS candidates
UNWIND candidates AS cand
// Exclude direct coauthors
WITH ch, cand
WHERE NOT EXISTS {
  MATCH (a:Article)-[:AUTHOR]->(ch), (a)-[:AUTHOR]->(cand)
}
// Find shared coauthors z between ch and cand
MATCH (a3:Article)-[:AUTHOR]->(ch), (a3)-[:AUTHOR]->(z:Author)
WHERE z <> ch
MATCH (a4:Article)-[:AUTHOR]->(cand), (a4)-[:AUTHOR]->(z)
WITH cand, collect(DISTINCT z) AS commonNeighbors
UNWIND commonNeighbors AS z
// Compute degree of z in the co-author graph (number of distinct coauthors)
MATCH (a5:Article)-[:AUTHOR]->(z), (a5)-[:AUTHOR]->(co:Author)
WHERE co <> z
WITH cand, z, count(DISTINCT co) AS degZ
WHERE degZ > 1
WITH cand, sum(1.0 / log(degZ)) AS aa
WHERE aa > 0
RETURN cand.name AS name
ORDER BY aa DESC, name ASC
LIMIT 3

raw_results.question: Chao Zhang has never co-authored with certain researchers who nonetheless share a co-author with them. Among these indirect connections, find the 3 most likely future collaborators, where a shared co-author counts more if that co-author has fewer total collaborators overall. Report only the top 3 names as a list of strings, breaking ties by name ascending and nothing else.

parameters.query: MATCH (a:Author {name: $name}) RETURN count(a) AS cnt

MATCH (cz:Author {name: $name})
MATCH (cz)-[:CO_AUTHORED]-(a:Author)-[:CO_AUTHORED]-(c:Author)
WHERE c <> cz AND NOT (cz)-[:CO_AUTHORED]-(c)
WITH c, a
MATCH (a)-[:CO_AUTHORED]-(other:Author)
WITH c, a, count(DISTINCT other) AS deg
WITH c, sum(1.0/deg) AS score
ORDER BY score DESC, c.name ASC
RETURN c.name AS name
LIMIT 3

raw_results.question: Find the top 5 authors involved in the most closed collaboration triangles, based on a co-authorship graph where an edge exists between two authors if they have co-authored at least one paper. If ties occur at the cutoff, break ties by name ascending. Report only the names as a list of strings and nothing else.

parameters.query: MATCH (a:Author)-[r:CO_AUTHORED]-(b:Author) RETURN count(r) AS cnt
MATCH (a:Author) WHERE exists(a.name) RETURN count(a) AS cnt
MATCH (a:Author) WHERE a.name IS NOT NULL RETURN count(a) AS cnt

CALL gds.graph.nodeProperty.stream('coauthor_graph', 'triangleCount')
YIELD nodeId, propertyValue AS triangles
WITH gds.util.asNode(nodeId) AS n, triangles
WHERE n:Author
RETURN n.name AS name, triangles
ORDER BY triangles DESC, name ASC
LIMIT 10

raw_results.question: Based on a co-authorship graph where an edge exists between two authors if they have co-authored at least one paper, how many authors are involved in more than 50 closed collaboration triangles? Report only the number and nothing else.

parameters.query:
CALL gds.graph.nodeProperty.stream($g, $prop) YIELD nodeId, propertyValue
WITH propertyValue WHERE propertyValue > 50
RETURN count(*) AS c

raw_results.question: Find the top 5 articles with the highest PageRank score based on citations and report only the titles as a list of strings and nothing else.

parameters.cypherQuery:
MATCH (n:Article)-[r:CITED]->(m:Article)
RETURN gds.graph.project(
 $graph_name,
 n,
 m,
 {
  sourceNodeLabels: labels(n),
  targetNodeLabels: labels(m),
  relationshipType: type(r)
 }
)

parameters.query:
CALL gds.pageRank.stream($g) YIELD nodeId, score
RETURN gds.util.asNode(nodeId).title AS title, score
ORDER BY score DESC
LIMIT 5

raw_results.question: Compute the mean shortest path distance following outgoing CITED edges from the article "A practical guide for using statistical tests to assess randomized algorithms in software engineering" to all articles reachable from it. Round to 3 decimal points. Report only the number and nothing else.

parameters.query: MATCH (a:Article {title: $t}) RETURN count(a) AS c

params.t: A practical guide for using statistical tests to assess randomized algorithms in software engineering

parameters.cypherQuery:
MATCH (n:Article)-[r:CITED]->(m:Article)
RETURN gds.graph.project(
  $graph_name,
  n,
  m,
  {
    sourceNodeLabels: labels(n),
    targetNodeLabels: labels(m),
    relationshipType: type(r)
  }
)

parameters.sourceNode: A practical guide for using statistical tests to assess randomized algorithms in software engineering

parameters.query:
MATCH (n:Article {title: $t})
CALL gds.shortestPath.dijkstra.stream('article_cited_graph', { sourceNode: id(n) })
YIELD totalCost
WITH totalCost
WHERE totalCost > 0 AND gds.util.isFinite(totalCost)
RETURN round(avg(totalCost), 3) AS mean

params.t: A practical guide for using statistical tests to assess randomized algorithms in software engineering

parameters.sourceNode: A practical guide for using statistical tests to assess randomized algorithms in software engineering

parameters.query:
MATCH (n:Article {title: $t})
CALL gds.bfs.stream('article_cited_graph', { sourceNode: id(n) })
YIELD nodeId, depth
WITH depth
WHERE depth > 0 AND gds.util.isFinite(depth)
RETURN round(avg(depth), 3) AS mean

params.t: A practical guide for using statistical tests to assess randomized algorithms in software engineering

parameters.query:
MATCH (n:Article {title: $t})
CALL gds.bellmanFord.stream('article_cited_graph', { sourceNode: id(n) })
YIELD nodeId, distance
WITH distance
WHERE distance > 0 AND gds.util.isFinite(distance)
RETURN round(avg(distance), 3) AS mean

params.t: A practical guide for using statistical tests to assess randomized algorithms in software engineering

parameters.query:
MATCH (n:Article {title: $t})
CALL gds.bellmanFord.stream('article_cited_graph', { sourceNode: id(n) })
YIELD *
RETURN * LIMIT 1

params.t: A practical guide for using statistical tests to assess randomized algorithms in software engineering

parameters.query:
MATCH (src:Article {title: $t})
MATCH (src)-[:CITED*1..20]->(t:Article)
WITH DISTINCT t, src
MATCH p = shortestPath( (src)-[:CITED*1..20]->(t) )
WITH length(p) AS d
WHERE d > 0
RETURN round(avg(d), 3) AS mean

params.t: A practical guide for using statistical tests to assess randomized algorithms in software engineering

parameters.query:
MATCH (src:Article {title: $t})
MATCH (src)-[:CITED*1..50]->(t:Article)
WITH DISTINCT t, src
MATCH p = shortestPath( (src)-[:CITED*1..50]->(t) )
WITH length(p) AS d
WHERE d > 0
RETURN round(avg(d), 3) AS mean

raw_results.question: Run Eigenvector Centrality on the citation graph, using CITED relationships. Find the top 3 papers by eigenvector centrality, excluding only the single #1-ranked paper by PageRank. Report only the titles as a list of strings and nothing else.

parameters.cypherQuery:
MATCH (n:Article)-[r:CITED]->(m:Article)
RETURN gds.graph.project(
 $graph_name,
 n,
 m,
 {
  sourceNodeLabels: labels(n),
  targetNodeLabels: labels(m),
  relationshipType: type(r)
 }
)

parameters.query:
CALL gds.graph.nodeProperties.stream('citation_graph_cited', 'pr') YIELD nodeId, propertyValue AS pr
WITH nodeId, pr
ORDER BY pr DESC LIMIT 1
WITH nodeId AS excludeId
CALL gds.graph.nodeProperties.stream('citation_graph_cited', 'ec') YIELD nodeId, propertyValue AS ec
WHERE nodeId <> excludeId
RETURN gds.util.asNode(nodeId).title AS title, ec

raw_results.question: Build the co-authorship graph (edge = co-authored at least one article). Among authors with more than 5 collaborators, find the mean local clustering coefficient. Report only the number round to 3 decimal places and nothing else.

parameters.query:
MATCH (a:Author)-[:CO_AUTHORED]-(:Author)
WITH a, collect(DISTINCT a) as aa // dummy to keep a distinct only once
WITH a
MATCH (a)-[:CO_AUTHORED]-(b:Author)
WITH a, collect(DISTINCT b) AS neighbors, count(DISTINCT b) AS d
WHERE d > 5
UNWIND neighbors AS n1
UNWIND neighbors AS n2
WITH a, d, n1, n2
WHERE id(n1) < id(n2)
MATCH (n1)-[:CO_AUTHORED]-(n2)
WITH a, d, count(*) AS e_between_neighbors
RETURN avg( (2.0*e_between_neighbors) / (toFloat(d)*(d-1)) ) AS mean_lcc

raw_results.question: Find the number of distinct authors who are exactly 5 hops away from Chao Zhang, or exactly 5 hops away from Yihui Jin, in the co-authorship graph (edge = co-authored at least one article), and whose degree centrality — computed over the full co-authorship graph — is 5 or higher. Report only the number and nothing else.

parameters.query:
MATCH (a:Author {name: 'Chao Zhang'})-[:CO_AUTHORED*5]-(b:Author)
RETURN DISTINCT b.name AS name
UNION
MATCH (a:Author {name: 'Yihui Jin'})-[:CO_AUTHORED*5]-(b:Author)
RETURN DISTINCT b.name AS name

MATCH (s1:Author {name: 'Chao Zhang'})-[:CO_AUTHORED*5]-(b:Author)
WITH DISTINCT b
MATCH (s2:Author {name: 'Yihui Jin'})-[:CO_AUTHORED*5]-(b)
WITH COLLECT(DISTINCT b) AS b2
MATCH (s1:Author {name: 'Chao Zhang'})-[:CO_AUTHORED*5]-(b1:Author)
WITH b2 + COLLECT(DISTINCT b1) AS bs
UNWIND bs AS b
WITH DISTINCT b
MATCH (b)-[:CO_AUTHORED]-(c:Author)
WITH b, count(DISTINCT c) AS deg
WHERE deg >= 5
RETURN count(DISTINCT b) AS cnt

CALL {
  MATCH (s:Author {name:'Chao Zhang'})-[:CO_AUTHORED*5]-(b:Author)
  RETURN b
  UNION
  MATCH (s:Author {name:'Yihui Jin'})-[:CO_AUTHORED*5]-(b:Author)
  RETURN b
}
WITH DISTINCT b
MATCH (b)-[:CO_AUTHORED]-(c:Author)
WITH b, count(DISTINCT c) AS deg
WHERE deg >= 5
RETURN count(DISTINCT b) AS cnt

raw_results.question: For each venue, identify the article with the highest PageRank score (computed using only CITED relationships) among those published there. Across all these per-venue top articles, what is the mean PageRank score? Round to 3 decimal places. Report only the number and nothing else.

parameters.cypherQuery:
MATCH (n:Article)-[r:CITED]->(m:Article)
RETURN gds.graph.project(
  $graph_name,
  n,
  m,
  {
    sourceNodeLabels: labels(n),
    targetNodeLabels: labels(m),
    relationshipType: type(r)
  }
)

parameters.query:
MATCH (a:Article)-[:VENUE]->(v:Venue)
RETURN v.name AS venue, collect(a.index) AS indices

MATCH (a:Article)-[:VENUE]->(v:Venue)
RETURN v.name AS venue, count(*) AS cnt

MATCH (a:Article)-[:VENUE]->(v:Venue {name: $venue})
RETURN a.index AS index LIMIT 5
MATCH (a:Article)-[:VENUE]->(v:Venue {name: $venue}) RETURN count(*) AS cnt
MATCH (a:Article)-[:VENUE]->(v:Venue {name: $venue}) RETURN a.index AS index SKIP $skip LIMIT $limit

CALL gds.pageRank.stream($g) YIELD nodeId, score
WITH gds.util.asNode(nodeId) AS a, score
MATCH (a:Article)-[:VENUE]->(v:Venue)
WITH v.name AS venue, max(score) AS top
RETURN avg(top) AS meanTop
